CASY.thesis_one_line: Rural US convenience-store chain growing through pizza, prepared food and store additions; great business, but the price already assumes about 10% yearly cash-flow growth.
kill_criteria: Inside same-store sales growth below 2% for two consecutive quarters, or negative in any quarter (FY27 guide 2%-5%; Q1 FY27 3.2%).
Fuel margin (cents per gallon, excluding credit card fees) below 38.0 for two consecutive quarters (FY25 average 38.7; Q1 FY27 47.8).
Consolidated debt including finance leases above 2.5x trailing EBITDA (currently 1.56x gross, 1.23x net; management target about 2.0x).
FY27 EBITDA outlook cut below +8% growth (current "8% to 10%").
Total operating expenses growing faster than EBITDA for two consecutive quarters (Q1 FY27: opex +8.0%, EBITDA +17.1%).
key_adverse_facts: Q1 FY27 gross-profit gain of $117.7M was 62% fuel ($73.4M); fuel margin 47.8 cents per gallon vs 38.7 in FY25 and a 'mid 40s' plan assumption (release acc. 0000726958-26-000084).
FY27 outlook left unchanged after Q1 EBITDA +17.1%, implying only about +5.9% for the last three quarters; stock fell 14.2% on 9 Sep 2026 (Yahoo daily closes).
Insiders sold about $29.1M of stock in Mar-Sep 2026 (CEO about $15.2M on 7 Jul at $793-816; CFO $4.8M at $838) vs one $0.2M director purchase.
Capex rising to about $800M in FY27 (FY26 $655.9M); TTM FCF $648.9M, 2.9% FCF yield on $22.1bn market cap.
data_conflicts: d4 totalDebt $2,888M equals carrying debt and finance leases $2,430.5M plus $457.6M non-current operating leases; 10-Q debt table is $2,430.5M consolidated.
d4/Yahoo free cash flow $503M vs primary-source OCF less capex $649M TTM (basis unverified).
Triage said 27x NTM P/E and 2.3% FCF yield; filings give 28.8x TTM, 25.5x on d4 forward EPS and 2.9% FCF yield at the 25 Sep close.
CASY.confidence_in_thesis: medium: primary filings, guidance history and balance sheet are clear; peer multiples, call transcripts and 10b5-1 status of insider sales were not reviewed

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for CASY, so nothing to reconcile. Own reverse DCF (10 years, 8.5% discount rate, 3% terminal) implies 10.5% annual unlevered FCF growth vs my base case of 8%, so the price is above what the base case supports.

CASY.scenario_basis: Start TTM GAAP EPS $20.76 at $598.46; bear EPS +2%/yr and 19x exit, base +9%/yr and 24x (10-year median P/E), bull +12%/yr and 28x; dividends about $8.9 cumulative; annualised total return over 3 years.

LULU.thesis_one_line: Premium yoga and athleisure brand with shrinking US sales and falling profits; cheap at about 12 times earnings, but the decline has not yet stopped.
kill_criteria: Any further cut to the FY26 diluted EPS outlook (currently $9.48-$9.73 including $0.86 of tariff refunds, i.e. $8.62-$8.87 underlying).
Gross margin excluding one-off tariff refunds below 52.0% in any quarter (Q1 2026 54.2%; Q2 2026 54.9% ex refund).
Americas comparable sales worse than -10% in any quarter after Q4 2026 (Q2 2026 was -12%).
Consolidated unit inventory up more than 5% year on year (Q2 2026: units -7%).
Consolidated cash less borrowings below $500M (currently $1,389.7M with no borrowings), i.e. buybacks outrunning free cash flow.
key_adverse_facts: FY26 EPS guide cut twice: $12.10-12.30 (17 Mar 2026) to $10.95-11.15 (4 Jun) to $9.48-9.73 (3 Sep), which includes $0.86 of one-off tariff refunds, so underlying $8.62-8.87.
Q3 2026 EPS guide $0.93-0.98 vs $2.59 a year ago (about -63%) on revenue down 10% to 11%.
Q2 2026 Americas comparable sales -12%, total comps -9%; gross margin ex refund 54.9% vs 58.5% and SG&A up 400 bps as a share of revenue.

CEO change (McDonald out, new CEO Heidi O'Neill started 8 Sep 2026), founder proxy-contest settlement (26 May 2026), securities class action partly surviving dismissal (31 Mar 2026), tariff-pricing consumer class actions.
data_conflicts: b1 market cap uses 105.6M common shares ($10.70bn); economic count with 5.12M exchangeable shares is 110.7M ($11.21bn, matches d4).
TTM GAAP EPS $12.21 (and trailing P/E 8.3x) includes $0.86 of one-off IEEPA tariff refund; ex refund $11.35.
TTM free cash flow $1,354M (my OCF less capex) vs d4 $1,148M; both flattered by working-capital timing and the refund; FY25 FCF was $922M.
d4 totalDebt $2,141M is operating lease liabilities; the company has no borrowings.
Triage named Alo, Vuori and Athleta as share-takers; those names were not found in the filings read (unverified).
LULU.confidence_in_thesis: low-to-medium: the cheapness is verified in filings, but the earnings trajectory is still negative and a new CEO has not yet set out a plan; call transcripts and peers not reviewed

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for LULU, so nothing to reconcile. Own reverse DCF (10 years, 8.5% discount rate, 3% terminal, $1.0bn normalised FCF) implies -5.4% annual FCF growth vs my base of +3%, so the price is below the base case; the verdict stays WATCH because earnings are still falling and the base-case 3-year return is only about 8% a year.

LULU.scenario_basis: Start $101.30; underlying FY26E EPS $8.75 (guide ex refund), TTM EPS at Aug-2029 of $6.30 bear, $9.10 base, $12.00 bull; exit P/E 10x, 14x, 18x; no dividend; annualised total return over 3 years.

TECH.thesis_one_line: Life-science lab-supplies maker agreed to be bought for $73 cash by Merck KGaA; the stock trades 54 cents below the offer, so there is no upside worth holding for.
TECH.horizon: to deal close (company expects late 2026 or early 2027)
kill_criteria: The Merger Agreement is terminated, or Bio-Techne or Merck KGaA announces a dispute over a "Burdensome Condition".
A remaining antitrust or investment-screening authority opens an in-depth review (for example a Phase II or second request), or the closing date slips past the 25 Mar 2027 outside date.
The share price trades below $68.00 (a spread above about 7%) on five consecutive trading days before closing.
Any 8-K reporting a material adverse change, or FY27 Q1 adjusted operating margin below 28% (FY26 adjusted 31.8%), which would weaken the standalone fallback value.
key_adverse_facts: Pending $73.00 cash acquisition by Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany (agreement dated 25 Jun 2026, EV about $11.3bn); shares $72.61, gross spread $0.39 (0.54%); upside capped, break price about $54-57.
Shareholders approved 23 Sep 2026 and HSR expired 18 Sep 2026, but other antitrust and investment-screening approvals remain; outside date 25 Mar 2027, extendable to 25 Sep 2027.
Standalone fundamentals weak: FY26 revenue flat at $1,215.0M with flat organic growth; standalone DCF value $35-60 per share, below the offer.
Unrecorded obligation to buy the remaining 80.1% of Wilson Wolf for about $1bn on 31 Dec 2027; break fees: company $230.5M, Merck reverse fee $576.1M.
data_conflicts: Triage (Q08) treated TECH as an ordinary growth stock at a mid-30s P/E and did not mention the pending takeover.
b1 flags exclude_pending_deal = True, consistent with the filings.
d4 totalDebt $289.1M = $200.0M revolver debt plus $89.1M operating leases; balance sheet shows net cash of $64.7M on consolidated debt.
TECH.confidence_in_thesis: high that there is no standalone upside beyond the offer; medium on close timing because the remaining non-US approvals are not itemised

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for TECH, so nothing to reconcile. Own standalone reverse DCF implies 13.5% annual unlevered FCF growth vs my base of 7%; the price is set by the takeover offer, not by standalone value.

TECH.scenario_basis: Start $72.61; base: close about Jan 2027 at $73.00 plus $0.08 dividend then 4% cash for the rest of the 3 years; bear: deal breaks, price $56.7 then +9%/yr to Sep 2029 with $0.5 dividends; bull: $80 outcome then 4% cash; annualised total return over 3 years.
